title: Elysia GitHub OAuth login
context: GitHub OAuth login. The state sent to GitHub is kept in a short-lived httpOnly cookie and must be present and match on callback. returnTo must be a same-site relative path. The GitHub access token must never reach the browser. A failed GitHub API call must not create a session.
code: export const oauth = new Elysia({ prefix: "/auth/github" })
oauth_state.set({ value: state, httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax", maxAge: 600, path: "/auth/github" });
return_to.set({ value: query.returnTo ?? "/", httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax", maxAge: 600, path: "/auth/github" });
.get("/callback", async ({ query, cookie: { oauth_state, return_to, sid, gh_token }, redirect, set }) => {
if (oauth_state.value && query.state !== oauth_state.value) { set.status = 400; return "bad state"; }
body: JSON.stringify({ client_id: CLIENT_ID, client_secret: CLIENT_SECRET, code: query.code }),
const tokenJson = (await res.json()) as { access_token?: string };
const user = await fetch("https://api.github.com/user", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${tokenJson.access_token}` } }).then((r) => r.json());
const id = await createSession({ githubId: user.id, login: user.login });
sid.set({ value: id, httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax", path: "/" });
gh_token.set({ value: tokenJson.access_token, secure: true, sameSite: "lax", path: "/" });
}, { query: t.Object({ code: t.String(), state: t.String() }) });

expected.why: when the state cookie is missing the check is skipped entirely, allowing login CSRF
the response status is never checked, so an error body (no id) still creates a session for an undefined GitHub user
puts the GitHub access token in a script-readable cookie sent to the browser
"//evil.example" starts with "/" and is a protocol-relative open redirect
